s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive cutaneous eruption with hyperkeratotic papules
salient_findings: Reddish brown hyperkeratotic papules on the left leg
Slight bleeding after removal of scales
Compact hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate on biopsy
key_facts: 10-year history of slowly progressive cutaneous eruption
Eruption located on the front and back of the left leg
Papules are 1 to 10 mm wide
Patient has a 16-year history of diabetes mellitus
Diabetes is being treated with metformin
No history of another endocrine disorder or malignant neoplasm
No family history of similar cutaneous findings
Hematological and biochemical test results are unremarkable
Lesional skin biopsy shows compact hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate

shortlist.label: Lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate and epidermal atrophy are characteristic of lichen planus

shortlist.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: presence of hyperkeratotic papules and bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate are consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus

shortlist.label: Psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: hyperkeratotic papules and epidermal atrophy are features of psoriasis

shortlist.label: Lichenoid keratosis
shortlist.why_kept: clinical presentation of hyperkeratotic papules and histological findings of compact hyperkeratosis and bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate are consistent with lichenoid keratosis

shortlist.label: Granuloma faciale
shortlist.why_kept: presence of hyperkeratotic papules and bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate are features of granuloma faciale

raw.rationale: The clinical presentation of reddish brown hyperkeratotic papules and the histopathological findings of compact hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate are consistent with lichenoid keratosis, which is a benign skin condition that can present as a solitary lesion or multiple lesions, often on the legs.

rejected.label: Lichen planus
rejected.why: Lichen planus typically presents with multiple lesions, mucosal involvement, and a more widespread distribution, which is not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: Discoid lupus erythematosus is an autoimmune condition that typically presents with scarring lesions, often on the face, and is associated with other systemic symptoms, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Psoriasis
rejected.why: Psoriasis typically presents with well-demarcated, scaly plaques, often on the elbows, knees, and scalp, and is associated with other systemic symptoms, which are not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Granuloma faciale
rejected.why: Granuloma faciale is a rare condition that typically presents with a single lesion on the face, which is not consistent with the presentation in this case.
